Opposite Party :- State Of U.P. And 3 Others Counsel for Applicant :- Ghanshyam Tripathi,Ashutosh Tripathi Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Samit Gopal,J.
List revised.

Heard Sri Dharmendra Kumar Shukla, Advocate holding brief of Shri Ghanshyam Tripathi, learned counsel for the applicant, Shri S.B. Maurya, learned counsel for the State and perused the material brought on record.

The present application under Section 482 Cr.P.C. has been filed by the applicant- Sheshmani Pandey with the prayer to direct the court below to decide Case No. 4077 of 2010 (State of U.P. Vs.
Omkar Shukla and others) arising out of Case Crime No. 529 of 2010, under Sections 419 and 420 I.P.C. Police Station Badlapur, District Jaunpur pending before the A.C.J. (J.D.), N.I. 3rd, District Jaunpur as soon as possible within three months or pass such other and further orders which this Hon'ble Court deems fit and proper in the circumstances of the case otherwise the applicant shall suffer a irreparable loss and injury.

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the applicant argued that the applicant is the first informant of the present case.

It is further argued that the trial is lingering on just because of non co-operation of the opposite party no.2 and, as such, appropriate direction be issued for disposal of trial in time bound manner.

sentences.text: Per contra, learned counsel for the State opposed the prayer made in the present matter by arguing that no such specific reasons have been made out for giving any direction for expediting the trial of the case and as such the application be dismissed.
After hearing the learned counsel for the parties and perusing the records, it is evident that there is no specific reason for expediting the same.

However, the applicant who is the first informant may file an application for expediting the trial before the court concerned within two weeks from today which may as per its load of work, diary and pendency of cases pass appropriate orders on the same within two weeks.
It is made clear that this Court has not passed any direction for expediting the trial.
The present application is disposed of.
